title: Qluster Raises €4.7 Million Pre-Seed Round Led by Quantonation to Build Continuous-Variable Photonic Quantum Computers - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Paris photonic quantum startup Qluster, an LKB spin-out, raised a €4.7M pre-seed led by Quantonation (with Quantum Launchpad and Bpifrance) to build room-temperature continuous-variable cluster-state quantum computers, targeting an intermediate-scale system by 2032 and a fault-tolerant universal processor by 2036.

insights.claim: Paris-based photonic quantum computing startup Qluster closed a €4.7 million ($5.18 million) pre-seed round led by Quantonation, with participation from Quantum Launchpad and Bpifrance.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Marks Quantonation and French state-backed Bpifrance continuing to seed early-stage photonic quantum hardware in France; a data point on European quantum pre-seed round sizes.
insights.quote: Qluster has closed a €4.7 million ($5.18 million) pre-seed funding round led by Quantonation

insights.claim: Qluster plans to use its €4.7 million pre-seed capital to establish an independent R&D laboratory and expand its experimental physics and quantum architecture teams.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Capital goes to lab build-out and hiring, signalling a pre-product, research-stage company years from revenue.

insights.claim: Qluster is a spin-out of France's Laboratoire Kastler Brossel (Sorbonne Université, CNRS, École normale supérieure, Collège de France) and was previously backed by France 2030's 2026 i-Lab Grand Prize plus Agoranov, CNRS Innovation and Sorbonne Université startup programs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Illustrates France's public research-to-startup pipeline (France 2030, CNRS, Bpifrance) as a sustained source of quantum hardware deal flow.

insights.claim: Qluster's platform uses continuous-variable (CV) cluster states across spectrally multiplexed optical modes at room temperature, rather than encoding qubits in discrete single-photon paths.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Places Qluster in the CV-photonic camp, differentiated from discrete single-photon photonic approaches; track which photonic modality reaches scale first.
insights.quote: the platform uses continuous-variable (CV) cluster states across spectrally multiplexed optical modes at room temperature

insights.claim: Operating CV photonic cluster states at room temperature is intended to eliminate cryogenic infrastructure and simplify integration of quantum computers into data centers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: If room-temperature operation holds, it lowers deployment cost versus cryogenic modalities (e.g. superconducting), a potential competitive wedge for data-center adoption.
insights.quote: aiming to eliminate cryogenic infrastructure and simplify data-center integration

insights.claim: Qluster's hardware builds on patented miniature multimode squeezed-light source technology developed by co-founders Valentina Parigi and David Fainsin at Laboratoire Kastler Brossel.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Patented squeezed-light sources are the core IP moat; founder-held lab IP is the key diligence item for early photonic quantum startups.
insights.quote: patented miniature multimode squeezed-light source technology

insights.claim: Qluster uses an application-driven co-design methodology that maps target industrial workloads into circuit depth, logical qubit and power budgets before finalizing processor topology.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Workload-first co-design aims to tie hardware to commercially relevant use cases early; watch for named industrial partners as validation.
insights.quote: maps target industrial workloads into circuit depth, logical qubit, and power budgets prior to finalizing processor topology

insights.claim: Qluster targets an intermediate-scale quantum system by 2032 and a large-scale fault-tolerant universal processor by 2036.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A ~10-year path to fault tolerance means long-duration capital needs and multiple future dilutive rounds; benchmark against rival photonic roadmaps.
insights.quote: targets an intermediate-scale quantum system by 2032 and a large-scale fault-tolerant universal processor by 2036
